sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，你知道大卫·罗森汉（David Rosenhan），我们之前已经谈到过他，他，嗯，你知道，在他的书中写了关于在精神病院里保持理智与疯狂的经历。

sentences.en: Um, you have, you know, Joanna Moncrief who says like that the chemical imbalance theory about low serotonin and all that, that's just this myth.
sentences.zh: 嗯，还有，你知道的乔安娜·蒙克里夫（Joanna Moncrief），她说过，关于低血清素等化学失衡理论，那只是一种神话。

sentences.en: There's no evidence.
sentences.zh: 根本没有任何证据。

sentences.en: That's actually really, uh, for site, uh, she had a lot of foresight because the stuff

sentences.en: that's coming out now, they, they paid for all of this research, um, about 10 years ago that started coming out about, I don't know, six, five, six years ago.

sentences.zh: 其中大部分都在某种程度上证实了，所有的，嗯，我们之前都只是在猜测。

sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，要在正常和障碍之间划清界限真的很难。

sentences.zh: 我不会再多讲历史人物了。

sentences.zh: 我以前也谈过他，但是，你知道，他谈到了与人建立深刻的连接。

sentences.en: And so cause this was so healing and it was our humanity and our story.
sentences.zh: 因为这具有极大的疗愈作用，这就是我们的人性与我们的故事。

sentences.zh: 甚至即使那是精神病性的，如果你参与到某人的故事中，它就能开始让他们脚踏实地，并在关系上赋予他们活力。

sentences.zh: 解离性身份障碍（DID）的一个特点是，很多时候他们会感到极度不安全。

sentences.en: And then they start to remember more because it's not an intellectual, logical thing.
sentences.zh: 然后他们开始记起更多的事情，因为这不是一个纯粹靠理智和逻辑能解决的问题。

sentences.en: It's that their body is starting to be more safe.
sentences.zh: 而是他们的身体开始感到越来越安全。

sentences.en: They're starting to trust me and they're starting to calm down.
sentences.zh: 他们开始信任我，也开始平静下来。

sentences.en: And it doesn't matter if there's an intellectual memory of it because the safety is the point and the session is still
sentences.zh: 有没有关于这些事情的理性记忆并不重要，因为安全感才是核心，而且会谈依然

sentences.en: productive, you know, without me, um, delivering a whole lot of information that they remember

sentences.zh: 它不是我们告诉孩子该怎么做。

sentences.zh: 它不是靠我们说了什么。
